kurz: Fish is done when the flesh turns from translucent to opaque and separates easily into flakes, usually at 50–60 °C at the core (as a guide).
bild_im_kopf: Like a stack of playing cards: once cooked, a touch of the finger fans it into separate layers.
was_passiert: Fish protein changes at much lower temperatures than the meat of land animals. Its connective tissue is weak and gives way early. So fish is quickly cooked and quickly overcooked: a few degrees decide between juicy and dry.
warum_wichtig: Because fish keeps cooking, take it off when the middle is still just slightly translucent.
faustregeln: Better a minute too early than too late: fish keeps cooking.
schritte: Press gently into the thickest part with a fork.
If the flesh separates into flakes and is only a touch translucent inside, it is done.
With a thermometer: salmon at about 50 °C, white fish at 55–60 °C (as a guide).
